issues: Effect-type mismatch: the frame reads like a glass/shard scene with an overexposed emissive patch, not an explosion/fireball.
Severe highlight clipping/overexposure in the core (pure white with hard transitions), which kills fire detail and looks non-physical.
Missing volumetrics: no convincing smoke envelope, scattering, self-shadowing, or multi-scale billowing forms typical of explosions.

Reference comparison (auto-selected explosion reference): very low similarity—reference has dense volumetric fire+smoke, rich structure, and particulate detail; this render does not.
suggestions: (Most important) Switch to an actual explosion workflow: simulate/render a volumetric fire+smoke element (pyro/VDB) and drive emission from temperature/heat, not from flat emissive geometry.
Adopt HDR + proper tonemapping: render to 16/32-bit EXR and use Filmic/ACES so the core stays bright without clipping; add bloom/glare in comp rather than letting the beauty pass blow out.

Build a two-layer volume: (1) short-lived luminous flame volume (high emission, lower absorption), (2) longer-lived darker smoke volume (higher absorption, more scattering) with internal self-shadowing.
Add multi-scale turbulence: combine low-frequency large lobes + higher-frequency detail noise so the silhouette becomes “cauliflower/mushroom cloud” rather than sharp/rectilinear shapes.
Add secondary particles: embers/sparks (additive, short lifetime) + fine dust/ash (longer lifetime) + a range of debris sizes; enable motion blur for fast fragments in animation renders.
Improve scene lighting response: ensure the explosion actually lights nearby objects (warm fill/rim, spec hits on surfaces) and that smoke/volume casts shadows onto the environment.
